Maria G: quick sanity check: for the public API are we enforcing TLS 1.3+ and disabling TLS1.2? audit asked for confirmation. also who owns the rotation cadence for the edge certs (letsencrypt -> internal)?

AJ: yes — we've been TLSv1.3 only on the front doors since the Q4 infra push. cert rotation is handled by cert-manager for k8s/lets-encrypt; ops owns vault-backed certs for Dedicated/Private.

Dmitry: confirm on ciphers: only AEAD suites (CHACHA20-POLY1305 + AES-GCM). I ran a quick check this morning, no TLS1.2 accepted.

Maria G: @AJ can you paste the exact nginx config line that we can give to compliance? they want protocol + cipher policy.

AJ: sure — snippet below (front proxy):
```
# nginx tls settings
ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;
ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off;
# TLS1.3 ciphers negotiated by TLS stack; AEAD-only suites enforced via BoringSSL build flags
```

ops-bot: cert-manager:renew-job api.redwood.cloud — renewal succeeded for api.redwood.cloud (2026-03-10).

Kate: quick logging question — do our TLS handshake logs include client IPs or cert subjects? auditors asked to avoid shipping raw client IPs to the ELK retention window.

Dmitry: we log source IPs at the LB level. downstream log-forwarder redacts last octet for public traffic by default, but Dedicated customers' logs are preserved for support flows. need to check for any debug-level dumps.

sec-bot: policy reminder: PII and network identifiers must be redacted before cross-team sharing. See /policies/logging-redaction for the checklist.

Logan: who owns the KMS key that wraps the edge private keys? rotation window is 90 days, but we have an urgent compliance ask to rotate earlier — can we approve emergency rotation tomorrow morning?

Maria G: I can approve emergency rotation for edge keys if ops confirms no downtime. @AJ can you validate hot-rotate path and update secrets-manager?

Kate: I approve (responding as security reviewer). oncall will monitor cert validation windows. please tag the incident channel if any certs fail post-rotate.

AJ: :thumbsup: I'll take point. I'll coordinate the key rotation, update the secrets entries, and run post-rotation sslscan. I'll post results here.

Dmitry: ran sslscan after a quick rotate trial in staging — output: 
```
Host: api.staging.redwood.cloud:443
  TLSv1.3: yes
  Accepted  ciphers: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256
  No TLS1.2 fallback detected
```

Maria G: thanks — filing a short note in the compliance ticket with these confirmations and linking the cert-manager/rotation job. tagging @sec-bot to record the emergency rotation approval.

sec-bot: Recorded: compliance note created (https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-2026-1543).
